questions.question: In processor instruction set architecture (ISA) design, what is the defining characteristic of a 'load-store architecture' (such as classic RISC ISAs like MIPS, ARM, and RISC-V)?
options: Memory operands are directly referenced and modified by all arithmetic and logical operations to reduce register pressure.
Arithmetic and logical instructions operate exclusively on registers, with dedicated instructions specifically required to transfer data between memory and registers.
The processor eliminates hardware data caches entirely by streaming loads and stores directly to main memory.
Instructions must access memory in strict program order without allowing out-of-order execution or branch prediction.
Every arithmetic instruction is paired with two memory addresses to load inputs and store outputs in a single clock cycle.

questions.question: In low-power digital IC design, why is an Integrated Clock Gating (ICG) cell standardly implemented using an active-low latch paired with an AND gate, rather than a simple 2-input AND gate driven directly by the clock and enable signals?
options: To prevent glitches or runt pulses on the gated clock output if the enable signal transitions while the clock is high.
To double the clock frequency delivered to downstream sequential logic during active computation cycles.
To completely cut off static leakage current in downstream standard cells when disabled.
To perform automatic voltage level-shifting when crossing between heterogeneous power domains.
To generate a 90-degree phase shift required by dual-edge triggered flip-flops.

questions.question: In Tomasulo's algorithm for dynamic out-of-order instruction scheduling, what is the primary operational role of the Common Data Bus (CDB)?
options: It provides a dedicated point-to-point interconnect between the L1 data cache and integer execution units to bypass memory latency.
It enforces strictly in-order instruction retirement into the architectural register file to guarantee precise exceptions.
It translates virtual memory addresses to physical addresses directly inside reservation stations.
It serializes speculative branch condition checks to prevent pipeline flushes.
It broadcasts execution results tagged with reservation station IDs to all waiting reservation stations and register files simultaneously.

questions.question: In scan-based Design for Testability (DFT), why are 'lockup latches' standardly inserted between adjacent flip-flops in a scan chain that cross different clock domains or branches of a clock tree with substantial clock skew?
options: To compress test responses into compact multi-bit signatures for built-in self-test (BIST) analysis.
To convert serial test vector patterns into parallel vectors at the boundary of core logic blocks.
To eliminate combinational feedback loops during normal mission (functional) execution mode.
To protect the shift path against hold-time violations caused by clock skew during scan shift mode.
To restore degraded signal voltage levels on long scan enable routing lines across the die.

questions.question: In GPU Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT) architectures, what is 'branch divergence', and how does the microarchitecture typically handle it when threads within a single warp or wavefront take different paths at a conditional branch?
options: Divergent thread paths are distributed concurrently across distinct GPU compute cores via hardware-managed thread migration.
The hardware halts the entire warp and raises an architectural exception for the host CPU to resolve the branch sequentially.
The divergent paths are serialized and executed sequentially, while inactive threads for each path are disabled using an execution (predicate) mask.
Speculative execution is aborted across the entire warp, rolling all threads back to the nearest synchronization barrier.
The compiler forks the divergent threads into two independent unsynchronized warps that permanently divide the available shared memory allocation.
